# Dialect rows

Each row is a rule where GitHub and CommonMark 0.31.2 give a document a
different meaning (design 2.1). markfmt follows CommonMark 0.31.2 for core
constructs, and GitHub where a GFM construct decides. Each row names an input,
markfmt's result, GitHub's result, the GitHub fixture in `github/github.txt`
that shows GitHub's result, and the markfmt test of the rule. Where markfmt
and GitHub differ, `github/grammar-differs.txt` lists the fixture with a case
of markfmt's result (design 11.4). Each row has a dialect predicate in
`dialect.go`, which finds a span of the row in the row's GitHub fixture
(design 10.4).

| Rule | Input | markfmt | GitHub | GitHub fixture | markfmt test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HTML block kind 6 tag list: `search` is in the list, `source` is not | `a⏎<search>⏎*b*` | Paragraph `a`, then an HTML block `<search>⏎*b*` | Paragraph `a⏎<search>⏎*b*` with raw HTML and emphasis: `<search>` is kind 7, which cannot interrupt a paragraph | `dialect/html-block-search` | `TestParse/interrupts_a_paragraph_with_a_search_html_block` |
| HTML block kind 6 tag list: `source` is kind 7 | `a⏎<source>⏎*b*` | Paragraph `a⏎<source>⏎*b*` with raw HTML and emphasis | Paragraph `a`, then an HTML block `<source>⏎*b*` | `dialect/html-block-source` | `TestParse/does_not_interrupt_a_paragraph_with_an_html_block_of_kind_7` |
| HTML block kind 7 on a lazy candidate line: kind 7 does not start while a paragraph is open, matched or not | `> a⏎<del>⏎*b*` | Block quote with paragraph `a⏎<del>⏎*b*`: the lines are lazy | Block quote with paragraph `a`, then an HTML block `<del>⏎*b*` | `dialect/html-block-lazy-line` | `TestParse/does_not_start_an_html_block_of_kind_7_on_a_lazy_line` |
| Setext underline after link reference definitions alone: the line is paragraph text, and no other block starts on it, as in cmark 0.31.1. commonmark.js 0.31.2 gives an empty paragraph and a thematic break | `[foo]: /url⏎---` | Definition, then the paragraph `---` | The same as markfmt | `dialect/definition-underline` | `TestParse/adds_an_underline_after_definitions_alone_to_the_paragraph_as_text` |
| Raw HTML comment: `<!--`, text without `-->`, and `-->`; or `<!-->`; or `<!--->` (CM 626) | `a <!--> b --> <!-- c -- d --->` | Paragraph with the raw HTML `<!-->`, the text ` b --> `, and the raw HTML `<!-- c -- d --->` | Paragraph with the raw HTML `<!-->`, then the text ` b --> <!-- c -- d --->`: comment text must not contain `--` | `dialect/html-comment` | `TestParse/gives_raw_html_comments,_processing_instructions,_declarations_and_cdata_sections` |
| Unicode punctuation for flanking: Unicode P and S, and U+FFFD, which is So. The rule decides every `*`, `_` and `~` run | `£_a_£`, `£~!a~` | Paragraph with the emphasis `a`, and paragraph with the strikethrough `!a` | Paragraph `£_a_£`, and paragraph `£~!a~`: only Unicode P and ASCII punctuation count, so the run is not preceded by punctuation | `dialect/flanking-symbol` | `TestParse/treats_unicode_symbols_and_u+fffd_as_punctuation_for_flanking`, `TestTree_DialectSpans/finds_a_strikethrough_delimiter_run_next_to_a_unicode_symbol` |
| HTML block kind 4 start: `<!` and any ASCII letter | `<!doctype html>` | HTML block | Paragraph with the text `<!doctype html>`: the kind 4 start and the declaration grammar need an uppercase letter | `dialect/html-block-declaration` | `TestParse/starts_an_html_block_of_kind_4_with_any_ascii_letter` |
| Paragraph split off above a table: its lines get the cell pipe rule of the table (design 5.4). CommonMark 0.31.2, which has no tables, gives the text `a\|b c\\|d` and the code span `e\\|f` | ``a\\|b c\\\|d `e\\|f`⏎\| x \|⏎\| - \|`` | Paragraph with the text `a\|b c\|d` and the code span `e\|f`, then a table | The same as markfmt | `tables/split-paragraph` | `TestParse/gives_cell_pipe_escapes_in_text,_a_code_span,_a_destination_and_the_paragraph_above_a_table` |
| List items that start on one line: cmark 0.31.1 opens every one, and cmark-gfm opens at most 99 blocks on a line (`MAX_LIST_DEPTH`) | `- `×100 `a` | 100 nested lists, the last item with the paragraph `a` | 99 nested lists, the last item with the paragraph `- a` | `dialect/list-items-on-one-line` | `TestParse/opens_every_list_item_that_starts_on_a_line` |
| Footnote reference whose `^` is a backslash escape or an entity reference: its decoded text starts with `^` (design 6.3) | `a[\^1] b[&#94;1]⏎⏎[^1]: x` | Two references to the definition `1` | Garbled text `a[^1]] b[^`: cmark-gfm reads the label from the bytes after the node that holds the `^` | `footnotes/escaped-caret` | `TestParse/gives_a_footnote_reference_whose_caret_is_an_escape_or_an_entity_reference` |
| Footnote reference label across a line ending | `a[^b⏎c]⏎⏎[^b]: x` | An unresolved reference, written as its text `[^b⏎c]` | Garbled text `a[^]` | `footnotes/label-line-ending` | `TestParse/gives_a_footnote_reference_label_across_a_line_ending` |
| Code span after an unmatched backtick run: every later backtick run of the same length can close a code span. markfmt follows the spec text and commonmark.js 0.31.2, not cmark 0.31.1 | ``` a `` b `c` d `e` ``` | Paragraph with the code spans `c` and `e` | Paragraph with the code span `c` and the text `` `e` ``: the search for a closer misses a run that an earlier search recorded | `dialect/code-span-unmatched-run` | `TestParse/finds_every_closing_backtick_run_after_an_unmatched_run` |
| Link destination with VT or FF: VT and FF end a destination, as in cmark 0.31.1 (design 8.4) | `[a](b`, a form feed, `c)` | Paragraph with the text `[a](b`, a form feed and `c)` | Paragraph with a link to `b%0Cc`: cmark-gfm ends a destination only at a space, a tab or a line ending | `dialect/destination-vt-ff` | `TestParse/takes_control_characters_other_than_space,_tab,_vt_and_ff_in_a_destination,_and_del_in_an_angle_autolink` |
| Link reference definition whose title other characters follow on its line: the definition has no title (CM 210). markfmt follows the spec text and commonmark.js 0.31.2, not cmark 0.31.1 | `[foo]: /url⏎"title"ok⏎⏎[foo]` | The paragraph `"title"ok`, then a link to `/url` without a title | The same paragraph, then a link with the title `title` | `dialect/definition-failed-title` | `TestParse/rewinds_a_failed_title_to_the_end_of_the_destination` |
| Link label length: at most 999 characters. markfmt follows the spec text and commonmark.js 0.31.2; cmark 0.31.1 counts at most 1000 bytes | `[`, `é`×600, `]: /u⏎⏎[`, `é`×600, `]` | A definition and a link | Paragraphs with the text: the label has more than 1000 bytes | `dialect/label-length` | `TestParse/takes_a_label_of_999_characters` |
| Link label with VT or FF: VT and FF are whitespace, as in cmark 0.31.1 (design 6.7, 8.4) | `[a]⏎⏎[a`, a form feed, `]: /u` | A link to `/u` | The text `[a]`: cmark-gfm keeps VT and FF in a label | `dialect/label-vt-ff` | `TestParse/matches_a_link_label_with_ff_at_its_end,_as_cmark_does` |
| Info string with VT or FF at its ends: VT and FF are trimmed, as in cmark 0.31.1 (design 8.4) | `~~~`, a form feed, `a`, then a line and `~~~` | Fenced code with the info string `a` | Fenced code with the info string of a form feed and `a`: cmark-gfm trims only spaces and tabs | `dialect/info-string-vt-ff` | `TestParse/trims_vt_and_ff_from_an_info_string,_as_cmark_does` |
